items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The stars of this show were Felix Leclerc... Felix Leclerc was a very quiet and nice person to be with.

ctx.x: In between the time that Bolling had to wait before opening at the club St. Germain, a proposition came to me to do a 7 days tour with a show that was organized by Jacques Canetti, whc was the booking agent that had booked Louis Armstrong's first tour in France in 1934. It was through the grace of a French drummer named Gerard Pochonet that I got this gig. I had done some gigs with Pochonet before. He spoke very good English and admired American Negro musicians. He was a go getter and nice drummer also. Bill…

The stars of this show were Felix Leclerc, a French Canadian Singer and composer and André Claveau, who was a very popular music hall and radio singer. Another person who was to become a big star later was a comedian named Fernand Raynaud.

Jack Gauthier was quite well known fantasist and singer. Rose Mania was also with the show; a woman named Paulette Lancry and a couple of duettists named Vared and Bailly made up the rest of the show. We played the first four dates in Belgium, then we went to Lille, Roubaix and Bethune. Our success with the public was as great, if not greater than the stars, and we were put under a certain pressure by Rose Mania and Henri Lecca. We went on before Rose and di only three numbers, closing with the Saint Louis Blues.…
